--- title: "[Graph.single_source_shortest_path_length()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the shortest-path distance from one node to every node it can reach. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L41753-L41866){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.single_source_shortest_path_length( source, cutoff=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Single-source shortest path lengths](/assets/graphs/single-source-shortest-path-length.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The directed weighted graph with the source A outlined and each node's distance from A in a badge: A 0.0, B 1.0, E 2.0, C and D 3.0, and F 4.0, reached along the accent edges. The table lists the same distances from nearest to farthest." width="100%"} Runs one search from `source=` and records how far away every reachable node is: the number of hops on an unweighted graph, or the lowest total edge weight (Dijkstra's algorithm) on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`). Directed graphs are followed in edge direction. Distances from a single point of interest are useful for: - ego-network analysis ("everyone within two steps of this person") - service areas and catchments ("which stations are within 10 minutes") - shading or sizing nodes by how far they are from a focal node ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only include nodes at distance at most this value. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store distances in. If `None` (default), uses `"single_source_shortest_path_length"`. Nodes that are not reached get a null value. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the distances as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int | float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping each reachable node ID to its distance (`int` hops on an unweighted graph, `float` on a weighted graph); the source maps to `0`. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the label does not exist in the graph, or a weighted graph has a negative edge weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Distances from one end of a path count up hop by hop: ::: {#cef0570f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) dist = graph.single_source_shortest_path_length("A", return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): d for n, d in sorted(dist.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2, 'D': 3, 'E': 4} ``` ::: ::: Without `return_dict=`, the distances are stored on the nodes; with `cutoff=` the nodes beyond it are left null: ::: {#1ea2479e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .single_source_shortest_path_length("C", cutoff=1, attr_name="near_C") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "near_C"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
